title: Finite-field evaluation with arbitrary model relations
statement:
Fix $p,a,q,k_0,k$ as in [def-weil-finite-field-fiber], let $m\geq1$, put $Q=q^m$ and $E=\mathbf F_Q\subset k$. Let $r\geq0$ and let $\mathfrak a$ be any ideal of $k_0[t_1,\ldots,t_r]$ [def-weil-pbc-mv-polynomial-ring]. Let $\mathfrak a_k$ be its extension to $k[t_1,\ldots,t_r]$ and set $S=\{\lambda\in E^r: f(\lambda)=0\text{ for every }f\in\mathfrak a\}$. Evaluation induces $k$-algebra isomorphisms
$$k[t_1,\ldots,t_r]/(t_1^Q-t_1,\ldots,t_r^Q-t_r)\simeq\prod_{\lambda\in E^r}k,\qquad k[t_1,\ldots,t_r]/(\mathfrak a_k,t_1^Q-t_1,\ldots,t_r^Q-t_r)\simeq\prod_{\lambda\in S}k.$$
Under the first isomorphism, the extended ideal generated by $\mathfrak a_k$ is the product of the coordinate ideals $(f(\lambda):f\in\mathfrak a)\subseteq k$. These coordinate ideals are zero for $\lambda\in S$ and the unit ideal for $\lambda\notin S$. The set $S$ is finite and is canonically identified with $\operatorname{Hom}_{k_0\text{-alg}}(k_0[t_1,\ldots,t_r]/\mathfrak a,E)$ by the values of the coordinate classes; projection onto the corresponding factor $k$ in the second isomorphism is the scalar extension of that algebra map. For $r=0$ the indexing set $E^0$ is the singleton empty tuple; an empty surviving set gives the zero algebra. Both isomorphisms include their stated evaluation maps, not just abstract algebra isomorphisms. Here an ideal of a ring $R$ is an additive subgroup stable under multiplication by elements of $R$; $(S)$ denotes the ideal of finite sums of ring multiples of elements of $S$, and $R/L$ is the quotient by $u\sim v\iff u-v\in L$.

proof.text: Put E = D.extensionSubfield m hm. The unique-subfield theorem gives Nat.card E = q^m and compatibility of its base embedding with E.subtype. Positivity of q^m makes E finite. Inside E[X], Mathlib FiniteField.roots_X_pow_card_sub_X identifies the roots multiset of X^(card E)-X with the complete enumeration of E. The polynomial is monic since card E > 1. Polynomial.prod_multiset_X_sub_C_of_monic_of_roots_card_eq therefore gives its product factorization. Applying Polynomial.eval₂RingHom with coefficients mapped through E.subtype and X sent to t_i gives t_i^(q^m)-t_i = product over c in E of (t_i-c). This uses the finite-field root calculation directly, without a separate factorization in the algebraic closure.

source.place: Step 2, factorization of the finite-field polynomials

proof.text: By [def-weil-pbc-mv-polynomial-ring], evaluation defines a $k$-algebra map $v:P\to k^T$, $v(f)_\lambda=f(\lambda)$. Every generator of $J$ vanishes at every tuple in $T$ by [lem-weil-finite-field-pow-card], hence $J\subseteq\ker v$. Conversely, if $v(f)=0$, apply [lem-trf-grid-vanishing-linear-combination] with $K=k$, $I=\{1,\ldots,r\}$ and each $A_i=E$. These subsets are finite and nonempty. Step 1 identifies its $g_i$ with $t_i^Q-t_i$, so its conclusion writes $f$ as a sum of multiples of the generators of $J$. Consequently $\ker v=J$.

source.place: Step 2, kernel of the stated evaluation map

proof.text: For each tuple x in T=E^r, use Mathlib MvPolynomial.indicator x over E, mapped coefficientwise to k. Its value is 1 at x and 0 at every other tuple, by eval_indicator_apply_eq_one, eval_indicator_apply_eq_zero and map_eval. Thus the polynomial sum over x of C(z_x) times the mapped indicator evaluates to any prescribed function z:T→k. This gives surjectivity. The kernel from Step 2 and Ideal.quotientKerAlgEquivOfSurjective give the first k-algebra equivalence, and quotientKerAlgEquivOfSurjective_mk gives its evaluation formula.

source.place: Step 2, explicit interpolation inverse and evaluation isomorphism

proof.text: Let v:P→k^T be evaluation. The coordinate projection of Ideal.map v (a_k) is exactly the span of the evaluated model relations, by Ideal.map_map and MvPolynomial.eval_map. Mathlib Ideal.piOrderIso identifies every ideal of a finite product with the product of its coordinate images. Applying its inverse identity proves Ideal.map v (a_k) = Ideal.pi L, where L_x is the coordinate ideal in the statement. The evaluation formula for the first equivalence identifies this map with e₁ composed with the quotient map.

source.place: Step 2, coordinate ideals of arbitrary model relations

proof.text: The compatibility E.subtype.comp extensionEmbedding = algebraMap k₀ k identifies evaluation in E with evaluation in k after the injective subtype map. On S all generators of L_x vanish, so L_x=0 by Ideal.span_le. Outside S a model relation has nonzero value, a unit of k, and Ideal.eq_top_of_isUnit_mem gives L_x=k. Restriction ρ:k^T→k^S is surjective by extension by zero, and its kernel is Ideal.pi L by these two coordinate-ideal calculations. Consequently ker(ρ.comp v) = comap v (map v a_k) = a_k + ker v = a_k+J, using Ideal.comap_map_of_surjective. The quotient first isomorphism theorem gives e₂ and its evaluation formula. This includes empty S.

source.place: Step 2, surviving factors and the second evaluation isomorphism

proof.text: The set $S$ is finite since $S\subseteq E^r$ and $E$ and $r$ are finite. Given $\lambda\in S$, the polynomial universal property [def-weil-pbc-mv-polynomial-ring] gives evaluation $k_0[t]\to E$; it kills $\mathfrak a$, hence $[f]\mapsto f(\lambda)$ is a well-defined $k_0$-algebra map $k_0[t]/\mathfrak a\to E$. Conversely any such map gives $\lambda_i$ as the image of $[t_i]$; for $f\in\mathfrak a$ its value $f(\lambda)$ is zero, so $\lambda\in S$. The two constructions are inverse: one recovers every coordinate, and maps agreeing on the coordinates and coefficients agree on every polynomial and hence every quotient class.

source.place: Step 2, identification with model algebra maps

proof.text: For the point map $\phi_\lambda:k_0[t]/\mathfrak a\to E$ just obtained, scalar extension to $k$ along $E\subset k$ sends $a\otimes c$ to $c\phi_\lambda(a)$. On a representative $\sum_\alpha c_\alpha t^\alpha\in P$ this is $\sum_\alpha c_\alpha\lambda^\alpha$, precisely projection onto the $\lambda$-coordinate of the second evaluation isomorphism. Thus the maps have the asserted pointwise meaning. When $r=0$, $T$ has its one empty tuple, $P=k$ and $J=0$; the empty product $b_{()}=1$ makes all preceding calculations valid. When $S=\varnothing$, Step 5 gives kernel $P$, and both the quotient and the empty product $k^S$ are the zero algebra. No nonzero-quotient assumption was used.

source.place: Step 2, scalar-extended point maps and empty-index cases

proof_origin.place: Step 2; formalized by S9 using finite-field roots, Mathlib indicator interpolation, the combinatorial Nullstellensatz, piOrderIso, and quotient first isomorphism theorems. The finite-subfield calculation replaces separate algebraic-closure factorization.

lean.statement: theorem finiteFieldRelationsEvaluation (D : FiniteFieldDatum.{u}) (m : ℕ) (hm : 1 ≤ m) (r : ℕ) (a : Ideal (MvPolynomial (Fin r) D.k₀)) : ∃ e₁ : (MvPolynomial (Fin r) D.k ⧸ finiteFieldRelationsIdeal D m r) ≃ₐ[D.k] ((Fin r → D.extensionSubfield m hm) → D.k), ∃ e₂ : (MvPolynomial (Fin r) D.k ⧸ (finiteFieldRelationsExtendedIdeal D r a ⊔ finiteFieldRelationsIdeal D m r)) ≃ₐ[D.k] (finiteFieldRelationsSolutions D m hm r a → D.k), ∃ points : finiteFieldRelationsSolutions D m hm r a ≃ FiniteFieldRelationsPointMaps D m hm r a, (∀ (f : MvPolynomial (Fin r) D.k) (x : Fin r → D.extensionSubfield m hm), e₁ (Ideal.Quotient.mk (finiteFieldRelationsIdeal D m r) f) x = MvPolynomial.eval (fun i ↦ (x i).val) f) ∧ (∀ (f : MvPolynomial (Fin r) D.k) (x : finiteFieldRelationsSolutions D m hm r a), e₂ (Ideal.Quotient.mk (finiteFieldRelationsExtendedIdeal D r a ⊔ finiteFieldRelationsIdeal D m r) f) x = MvPolynomial.eval (fun i ↦ (x.val i).val) f) ∧ Ideal.map (e₁.toRingHom.comp (Ideal.Quotient.mk (finiteFieldRelationsIdeal D m r))) (finiteFieldRelationsExtendedIdeal D r a) = Ideal.pi (finiteFieldRelationsCoordinateIdeal D m hm r a) ∧ (∀ x ∈ finiteFieldRelationsSolutions D m hm r a, finiteFieldRelationsCoordinateIdeal D m hm r a x = ⊥) ∧ (∀ x ∉ finiteFieldRelationsSolutions D m hm r a, finiteFieldRelationsCoordinateIdeal D m hm r a x = ⊤) ∧ (finiteFieldRelationsSolutions D m hm r a).Finite ∧ (∀ (x : finiteFieldRelationsSolutions D m hm r a) (i : Fin r), points x (Ideal.Quotient.mk a (MvPolynomial.X i)) = x.val i) ∧ (∀ (x : finiteFieldRelationsSolutions D m hm r a) (f : MvPolynomial (Fin r) D.k₀) (c : D.k), e₂ (Ideal.Quotient.mk (finiteFieldRelationsExtendedIdeal D r a ⊔ finiteFieldRelationsIdeal D m r) (MvPolynomial.C c * MvPolynomial.map (algebraMap D.k₀ D.k) f)) x = c * (D.extensionSubfield m hm).subtype (points x (Ideal.Quotient.mk a f)))
